content.title: Cincinnati Reds fall to Boston Red Sox on Opening Day | Replay
content.text: Updated March 26, 2026, 7:04 p.m. ETFor the fifth time in six years, the Cincinnati Reds grandiose celebration of Opening Day ended on the wrong side of the scoreboard.It was the Boston Red Sox who spoiled the Reds' March 26 home opener, pulling out a 3-0 victory in front of a sellout crowd of 43,897 fans at Great American Ball Park. Locked in a pitchers’ duel for the majority of the afternoon, the Red Sox used small-ball to plate the only run they would need off of Reds reliever Pierce Johnson in the seventh inning.Johnson surrendered a lead-off double to pinch-hitter Marcelo Mayer, who was then sacrificed to third on a bunt and scored on a single past a drawn-in infield by nine-hole hitter Ceddanne Rafaela. The Reds bats were silenced by Boston left-hander Garrett Crochet, who yielded just three hits and a pair of walks while striking out eight over six innings. Two of those three hits came courtesy of rookie Sal Stewart. He and Elly De La Cruz notched back-to-back singles to load the bases with only one out in the sixth, but Crochet ended the threat by striking out Eugenio Suárez and Spencer Steer. The lack of offense spoiled a solid start by Andrew Abbott, who was the first left-hander to start for the Reds on Opening Day since 1998. Abbott, who struggled this spring with an 11.72 ERA over six appearances, held Boston scoreless over six innings. He repeatedly pitched out of jams, stranding six Red Sox runners and erasing a few more with a pair of double plays. He said he was aware of the Opening Day hoopla but wasn't overly caught up in it."I was kind of focused," Abbott said. "I really didn't get to enjoy it a lot. ... To me, it's just another game. Take the ball and throw."He also cautioned that fans shouldn't overreact to an 0-1 start."It's a long season, as we know," Abbott said. "Fans are going to have a lot of opportunities to come see us play."The Red Sox added two insurance runs in the top of the ninth inning off of Reds reliever Connor Phillips to make it 3-0.Then, former Red Aroldis Chapman tossed a scoreless ninth inning for the save. Chapman moves into a tie for 11th on the all-time saves list (368) with former Red Sox closer Jonathan Paplebon.Here’s how the action unfolded at Great American Ball Park: Boston Red Sox shutout Reds on Opening Day | Replay Boston Red Sox 3, Reds 0 − FINALAroldis Chapman retired the Reds in order for his 368th career save. Reliever Pierce Johnson takes the loss for Cincinnati and Boston starter Garrett Crochet gets the win. More insurance runs for Red Sox | Red Sox 3, Reds 0, Bottom 9Brock Burke's first pitch of the season was looped into right field for an RBI single by Boston DH Jarren Duran to give the Red Sox a 3-0 lead. Now, closer Aroldis Chapman is coming on for the save opportunity against his former club. Red Sox add to lead after successful challenge | Red Sox 2, Reds 0, Top 9A full-count pitch to Roman Anthony was called strike 3, but a Boston ABS challenge turned that call into ball 4 and a walk. It extended the inning for Trevor Story, who just ripped an RBI single to left field to give the Red Sox a 2-0 lead. The Reds are going to the bullpen again, this time with left-hander Brock Burke taking the hill. Sal Stewart with 3 hits on Opening Day | Red Sox 1, Reds 0, Top 9Sal Stewart has three of the Reds' four hits today. He just doubled with two outs in the eighth inning but was left stranded when Boston reliever Garrett Whitlock struck out Eugenio Suárez. Connor Phillips will pitch the ninth inning for the Reds. Boston Red Sox go to bullpen | Red Sox 1, Reds 0, Top 8Garrett Crochet is in line for a win after Boston got the ice-breaking run across in the top of the seventh inning. Crochet's season debut is done after twirling six innings of three-hit shutout baseball with two walks and eight strikeouts.Red Sox reliever Justin Slaten came in and walked Tyler Stephenson to begin the seventh inning but then retired three straight. Red Sox strike first on Opening Day | Red Sox 1, Reds 0, Top 7Boston pinch-hitter Marcelo Mayer led off the seventh inning with a double just out of the reach of diving Reds' outfielder TJ Friedl. He was bunted to third and scored on Ceddanne Rafaela's RBI single to center to put the Red Sox in front, 1-0.Terry Francona is going to the bullpen again and left-hander Sam Moll is now on the bump to face the top of the Boston batting order. Andrew Abbott's day is done | Red Sox 0, Reds 0, Top 7Andrew Abbott is done after tossing six scoreless innings on Opening Day. The left-hander allowed seven hits, walked one and struck out four over 83 pitches.Right-hander Pierce Johnson is out of the bullpen to make his Reds debut. Reds leave the bases loaded | Red Sox 0, Reds 0, Top 7A walk by Matt McClain followed by singles from Elly De La Cruz and Sal Stewart loaded the bases for Eugenio Suárez with only one out.Suárez struck out swinging and Spencer Steer worked the count full before striking out, as well. We remain scoreless through six. Reds rookie Sal Stewart remains in game after getting hit by line drive | Red Sox 0, Reds 0, Bottom 5Sal Stewart was hit in the wrist on a hard-hit line drive by Roman Anthony. The rookie dropped his glove and held his wrist in pain as Anthony raced to first for his third hit of the game. Stewart was checked on by the Reds medical staff and remained in the game.Meanwhile, Andrew Abbott recovered and got out of another jam by striking out Trevor Story and Jarren Duran to add another zero on the board. Boston Red Sox win first ABS challenge | Red Sox 0, Reds 0, Top 5The first ABS challenge for Boston was a successful one as a pitch called a ball on Reds' third baseman Eugenio Suárez was ruled strike three upon review.Red Sox starter Garrett Crochet has retired eight consecutive Cincinnati hitters since walking Spencer Steer in the second inning. Reds-Red Sox remains scoreless | Red Sox 0, Reds 0, Top 4The first hit by the Reds this season belongs to rookie Sal Stewart, who laced a double to left center to open the second inning. He, along with Spencer Steer (walk), were left stranded there when Noelvi Marte struck out to end the frame. That's been the only threat for Cincinnati against Boston starter Garrett Crochet.Andrew Abbott has allowed five hits and a walk thus far but has kept Boston scoreless thanks to a pair of double plays. Andrew Abbott works out of trouble again | Red Sox 0, Reds 0, Bottom 2In their first trip through the batting order, the Red Sox have put five men on base but have nothing to show for it. Wilyer Abreu led off the second inning with an infield single, then catcher Carlos Narvaez singled to right field two batters later.Abbott then got 9-hole hitter Ceddanne Rafaela to ground into a 6-4-3 double play, and we remain scoreless at Great American Ball Park. Andrew Abbott gets out of jam | Red Sox 0, Reds 0, Bottom 1Boston hitters were aggressive in the opening inning, but Andrew Abbott ultimately got out of it unscathed despite a pair of hits and a walk.Boston third baseman Caleb Durbin grounded out to Matt McClain with two on to end the frame. Baseball season begins in Cincinnati as Reds, Red Sox underway at Great American Ball ParkA new Reds season has begun as starting pitcher Andrew Abbott fired a 93 mph fastball that Boston leadoff hitter Roman Anthony smacked up the middle for a single.The baserunner was erased two pitches later when Abbott got Red Sox shortstop Trevor Story to ground into a 5-4-3 double play. Andrew Abbott's start marks the end of 28-year streak for Cincinnati RedsWith Hunter Greene and Nick Lodolo on the IL to begin the season, Andrew Abbott will toe the slab this afternoon on Opening Day.Abbott's start will mark the first time in 28 years that the Reds started a left-handed pitcher on Opening Day. The last southpaw to do it was Mike Remlinger, who took the loss against the San Diego Padres in 1998 after allowing 3 runs (1 earned) over five innings. Boston Red Sox lineup for Opening Day vs. Cincinnati RedsThe Red Sox finished 89-73 last season and fell in three games in the American League Wild Card series to the New York Yankees.Here is manager Alex Cora's lineup for Opening Day in Cincinnati.Roman Anthony, LFTrevor Story, SSJarren Duran, DHWillson Contreras, 1BCaleb Durbin, 3BWilyer Abreu, RFIsiah Kiner-Falefa, 2BCarlos Narvaez, CCeddanne Rafaela, CFStarting pitcher: Garrett Crochet. Cincinnati Enquirer writers predict Reds seasonThe Enquirer's Gordon Wittenmyer, Pat Brennan and Jason Williams rundown their predictions for the Reds this season from total wins, Hunter Greene's return, Elly De La Cruz's stats and more. What is the Reds win total for the 2026 season?The Reds win total (over/under) for the 2026 season is 80.5 games, according to DraftKings Sportsbook.The Reds are +550 to win the NL Central. The Chicago Cubs (+110) are the favorites, followed by the Milwaukee Brewers (+235). What is the Cincinnati Reds record on Opening Day?Today marks the Reds 150th Opening Day game at home. The Reds are 71-77-1 in home openers and 9-14 at Great American Ball Park.The Reds have lost four of their last five Opening Day games at Great American Ball Park with the lone win coming in 2024 over the Washington Nationals. Terry Francona recalls Opening Day with Reds in 1987It's already been a better Opening Day for Terry Francona this time around after having to visit the dentist just hours before his managerial debut in Cincinnati last year.In his lone Opening Day as a Reds player in 1987, Francona started at first base and went 2-for-4 with a home run in an 11-5 win over the Montreal Expos at Riverfront Stadium."I remember that night a bunch of us went to dinner after the game and the waitress had my uniform on. I was like, 'I've arrived,'" Francona said. "They have the parade. I think back then they didn't even have school. It's always been a big deal." Terry Francona: "I wish Crochet's brother was pitching."Reds manager Terry Francona joked about Opening Day nerves and facing Boston left-hander Garrett Crochet to begin the year."I wanna try to enjoy Opening Day. I'll try. You show up to try to win. I wish Crochet's brother was pitching," Francona said.Crochet, an All-Star in back-to-back seasons, went 18-5 with a 2.59 ERA last season in 32 starts for the Red Sox.The Reds tagged Crochet for 8 hits and 5 runs over 6 innings last June, but the Red Sox jumped all over Chase Burns in a 13-6 win at Fenway Park. Cincinnati Reds Opening Day lineup vs. Boston Red SoxCheck out the Reds starting lineup for Opening Day against the Boston Red Sox here.This is the first-ever Opening Day meeting between the Reds and Red Sox. The Reds last opened against an American League team during the abbreviated 2020 season, beating the Detroit Tigers, 7-1. Eugenio Suárez talks Reds Opening Day, WBC title Fresh off of recording the game-winning double that lifted Venezuela to World Baseball Classic title, Eugenio Suárez will begin his second stint with the Reds on Thursday. Suárez brings a powerful bat back into the Cincinnati lineup after slugging 49 homers last season with the Mariners and Diamondbacks. "Our goal, obviously, is to make the championship, win the World Series and bring the happiness back to Cincinnati," Suárez said. "I think we have a really good group, a really good team. We just have to believe in each other and play hard every time."Suárez is 1-for-19 in six career Opening Day starts with the Reds. His lone hit was a home run off Jack Flaherty in the Reds’ 11-6 loss to the St. Louis Cardinals in 2021. Caleb Ferguson nearing return to Reds Caleb Ferguson, one of three Reds pitchers to begin the year on the injured list, had an MRI, has started a throwing program and will travel with the team on the first road trip, according to manager Terry Francona. Ferguson, who signed a one-year, $4.5 million contract with the club this winter, suffered a right oblique injury during Spring Training. Ferguson appeared in two games for the Reds during Spring Training. He has appeared in 333 career games over the past seven seasons and posted a 3.27 ERA across 25 outings with Seattle in 2025. Nick Lodolo updateReds starting pitcher Nick Lodolo has started throwing after a blister forced the left-hander to start the season on the injured list, according to manager Terry Francona.Lodolo is eligible to return from the IL on April 7. How to watch, stream, listen to Reds vs. Red Sox on Opening DayOpening Day is the first regular-season game to be broadcast on Fox 19 (WXIX-TV) in Cincinnati.Cincinnati-area Spectrum subscribers can watch the game on channels 304 and 1304. Fans in the Reds' regional TV territory can watch all locally distributed games on cable and satellite providers. Those games can be streamed on REDS.TV through the MLB app.Fans from outside the Reds' regional TV territory can watch by subscribing to MLB.TV.You can listen to Reds-Red Sox matchup on area affiliate networks WLW-AM 700 and WKFS-FM 94.5.If you purchase through our links, the USA Today Network may earn a commission.
